scope: Proposition 11.3 (An arbitrarily close step) of the manuscript “Smooth counterexamples to Yau's nodal upper bound in dimensions three and four” (preprints/Smooth-counterexamples-to-Yaus-nodal-upper-bound-in-dimensions-three-and-four-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 350 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8e4c129bdb0f2f45), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 57. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let h ∈ U and suppose h − g0 has compact support in P. For every smooth-topology neighborhood O of h, every N > 0, and every integer kmin, there are an integer k ≥ kmin, a metric e h ∈ O ∩ U, and a real eigenfunction t such that −∆e h t = Λkt, Λk > N, cHS(t) > N p Λk for a sign score S, and Λk is simple. Both e h − g0 and t − u0 k have compact support in P. The inequalities persist in a neighborhood of e h in the sense of Lemma 11.2.
